data.name: About_Description
data.value:
Browser Select is a utility to dynamically select the browser you want instead of just having one default for all links. similar to the prompt in android to choose a browser when a link in a non-browser app is clicked/touched. it may not be useful for everyone but it really helps when you use multiple browsers for different things (e.g. one with proxy and one without) and open many links from other applications (e.g. Messengers).
this is an open source application with GPL v2 license. feel free to report bugs or suggest a feature at GitHub.

data.name: HelpMain_Text
data.value:
BrowserSelect lets you choose a browser every time you click a link outside a browser (e-mail client, messenger, PDF file, ...) instead of always opening the same default browser. For this BrowserSelect must be set as the default browser: Settings > Default Browser > Set as Default Browser.
THE BROWSER LIST The link being opened is shown in the title of the window. You can: 1. Press Esc or click "x" to not open the link at all (e.g. if you clicked by mistake or a program opens a web page after installation). 2. Open the link in a browser: - click the icon of the browser, or - press one of the keys shown in parentheses under the icon: 1-9 by position, letters from the name of the browser, or the custom shortcut keys set in Settings > Browsers > Edit... - hold Shift while clicking (or pressing the key) to open the link in a private/incognito window; right-click an icon and choose "Open in Private Window" for the same. 3. Click "Always" under a browser to always open links of this website in that browser. This creates a rule in Settings > Auto Select Filters; to undo it, select the rule there, click Delete and then Apply.
AUTO SELECT RULES In Settings > Auto Select Filters BrowserSelect can choose the browser automatically, by domain, whole URL, path, keyword, file extension, the application the link was clicked in, or a regular expression. A rule can also open the link in a private window, pass extra arguments to the browser, show the browser list anyway, or ignore the link. Click "Help" in that section for details, or the link above the rule list for examples. Hold Alt while clicking a link (in another application) to skip all rules and choose the browser manually (can be turned off in Settings > Options).
SETTINGS - Browsers: Add... a portable browser or any program; Edit... the name, icon, shortcut keys and arguments of a browser; Remove a manually added browser; uncheck a browser to hide it; change the order with Sort (Manual uses the arrow buttons). - Refresh: BrowserSelect caches the list of installed browsers and profiles the first time it runs. After installing or removing a browser or profile, click Refresh next to the list of browsers. - Default Browser: Set as Default Browser; File types... registers BrowserSelect for .html and .url files. - Options: show only running browsers, skip the rules with Alt, Export... / Import... rules and settings to/from a .json file. - Update checker: checks the releases of snipeTR/BrowserSelect on GitHub. When a new version is available, this help button turns into an update button; after the update message BrowserSelect offers to download and run the new installer (the setup asks to close BrowserSelect if it is still running). - Language (bottom left): user interface language; it is used the next time BrowserSelect starts.
If you mostly use one browser but want some websites to open in another one (e.g. Firefox for everything but IE for the company website), add a rule "*" for your main browser and separate rules for the other websites.
You can always open BrowserSelect from the Start menu to change its settings.
data.comment: Text of the help window opened with the ? button of the selection window

data.name: HelpRules_Text
data.value:
Every rule has five columns:
Match: what part of the link the Pattern is compared to: - Domain: the host name, e.g. google.com, *.google.com, website.* or * (matches everything) - URL: the whole link with * and ? wildcards, e.g. github.com/myorg/* or https://*/login* - Path: the path of the link, e.g. /watch* or /docs/* - Keyword: comma separated words, the link must contain one of them, e.g. zoom, meet - Extension: file extension of the link or opened file, e.g. pdf, html - Source App: the application the link was clicked in, e.g. outlook.exe, slack, teams* - Regex: a .NET regular expression matched against the whole link
Pattern: the text the link is compared to (see Match). Comparisons are case-insensitive.
Browser: what happens when the pattern matches: a browser to open the link with, "display BrowserSelect" to always show the browser list, or "ignore URL (do nothing)" to not open the link at all.
Private: open the link in a private/incognito window. Arguments: extra command line flags for the browser (e.g. --incognito --disable-web-security).
Exact patterns are checked first, then wildcard patterns, and * last; rules with the same priority are checked from top to bottom (Move Up / Move Down). The first matching rule wins; if none matches, the browser list is shown.
To delete a rule select it and click Delete (or press the Del key). Changes are saved with Apply. "Link opened from" (bottom of the window) shows the application to use in Source App rules.
Note: you can open BrowserSelect manually from the Start menu to change the rules. Hold Alt while clicking a link to skip the rules and choose manually. More examples: the link above the rule list.
data.comment: Text of the rules help window (Help button in Settings > Auto Select Filters)
